title: Classic Cheeseburgers with Oven Fries
subtitle: juicy pan-seared cheddar burgers on toasted buns, with crispy homemade oven fries
imageAlt: A cheddar cheeseburger on a toasted bun beside golden oven fries on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 6 burgers: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Oven at 230°C (450°F) for the fries; they take longer than the burgers, so start them first.
Handle the beef as little as possible and press a dimple in each patty so it cooks flat.

items.name: russet potatoes
items.note: about 4, scrubbed, cut in 1 cm sticks

steps.title: Fries in
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F). Soak the potato sticks in hot tap water 10 minutes, drain and pat very dry. Toss with the oil, salt and paprika and spread in one layer on a large rimmed baking sheet lined with parchment. Bake 30–35 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Gently mix the beef with the Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Shape into 6 patties about 1.5 cm thick, slightly wider than the buns, with a dimple in the centre.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the patties in 2 batches, 4–5 minutes a side, until 71°C (160°F) in the centre. Lay a slice of cheddar on each for the last minute and cover the pan to melt it.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Toast the buns cut side down in the skillet 1 minute while the last batch rests.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Spread the buns with the mayonnaise and ketchup, then add lettuce, the burger, tomato and pickles. Serve with the fries.

fixIt.fix: Press a shallow dimple in the centre of each patty before cooking.
Dry them well after soaking, give them space on the sheet and bake until deep golden.
Don't press them with the spatula, and take them off at 71°C (160°F).

saleTip: Buns and ground beef are often on the same No Frills flyer before long weekends; freeze extra buns.
swap: Ground turkey patties: same method, cooked to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Cooked patties reheat well; pack buns and toppings separately.
doneness: 71°C (160°F) in the centre of each patty (Health Canada, ground beef). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested pan-seared burger and oven fry methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): lightly mixed 1.5 cm patties with a dimple, seared to 71°C; soaked potato sticks baked at 230°C.
prepAhead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead; stack with parchment between them.
Cut the potatoes and keep them in cold water in the fridge up to 1 day.
reheat: Patties covered in a skillet over medium-low 4–5 minutes, or in the microwave 1 minute, until 74°C (165°F). Fries in the air fryer at 200°C (400°F) 4 minutes.

basic.note: Salt-and-pepper burgers with cheddar, ketchup and pickles.

stepNotes.0: Basic: oil and salt only on the fries.

fancy.note: Bacon, caramelised onions and a burger sauce.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: before the burgers, cook the bacon crisp in the skillet and set aside; pour off the fat. Then cook the onion in the butter over medium 12–15 minutes until golden, and set aside.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: stir the mayonnaise, ketchup and chopped pickles together as burger sauce; top each burger with bacon and onions.

plating: Burger on a board or plate, skewered to hold it together.
Extra ketchup in a small bowl for the fries.

why.1-0: Lean beef keeps flare-ups and grease down; the Worcestershire keeps it savoury and juicy.
why.0-0: Soaking washes off surface starch, so the fries crisp instead of sticking.
why.1-7: Cheese melts best under a lid for the last minute.

funFact: The cheeseburger is often credited to a 16-year-old cook in Pasadena, California, around 1926.

keeps.note: freeze cooked patties with parchment between them
